extracted.intended_audience: digital newsroom editors, journalists, newsroom managers, and researchers in journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Operationalizing audience analytics into newsroom news-selection criteria and promotional decisions for digital newsrooms; summarizes metrics, how they map to editorial decisions, tensions, and implicit newsworthiness signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pageviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Gross visits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under Volume Metrics as a basic measure of traffic volume used by newsrooms to assess reach and past performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique visitors
rubrics_metrics.description: Reach (unique users visiting the site).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volume metric used to measure audience reach rather than repeat activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sessions per user
rubrics_metrics.description: Return visits (how often users return).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volume metric indicating user loyalty/recurrence; helpful for understanding repeat engagement patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pages per session
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery within site (how many pages a visitor views in a session).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Volume metric reflecting navigation depth and site discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dwell time
rubrics_metrics.description: Average time on page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as an Engagement Quality Metric; used as a proxy for depth of consumption and article value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scroll depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Percentage of article scrolled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement measure indicating how far users progress through an article; signals content consumption beyond initial click.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Reads (Chartbeat metric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Users reading at least half of article based on word length, time, average reading speed (Chartbeat's definition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly called out as an engagement-quality metric; used to identify substantive reads rather than superficial clicks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recirculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Clicks on related stories that pull users deeper into the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement metric indicating ability of a story to generate further internal traffic; implicated in loyalty and site stickiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active engaged time
rubrics_metrics.description: Time with focus on tab (active attention on the article).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement-quality metric intended to distinguish passive open tabs from active reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source of traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Where visits originate (search, social, direct, referral).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution metric used to understand acquisition channels and to shape headline, SEO, and distribution strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic origin
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic location of audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution metric used for geographic targeting and editorial decisions about regional relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device type
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of device used to access content (mobile, desktop, tablet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution metric affecting format and presentation choices (shorter mobile-friendly formats, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of arrival
rubrics_metrics.description: Time when users arrive at content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distribution metric used to time publication and promotional activity to match audience behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber stories
rubrics_metrics.description: What subscribers read (content consumption specifically by subscribers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loyalty/subscription metric used to understand and prioritize content that retains or appeals to paying audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion-driving stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that prompted subscriptions (content shown to convert non-subscribers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to identify editorial opportunities that generate revenue through subscriptions and inform promotional prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Email signups
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of newsletter/email registrations driven by content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscription metric used to gauge lead generation and direct-audience channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: App downloads
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of app installs attributed to content or campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Metric reflecting success in driving platform adoption and deeper audience relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Content shares by platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social metric indicating external propagation and potential earned reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: User comments on articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social engagement signal reflecting audience interaction and community response; may factor into editorial assessment of resonance and controversy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reactions
rubrics_metrics.description: Likes, reactions, and other simple social feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick social engagement metrics used as availability signals for popularity and sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past performance of similar stories
rubrics_metrics.description: How previously published, similar content performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used under 'What's Worth Covering Tomorrow?' — informs editorial decisions by analogizing likely audience response from historical patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic categories that drive subscribers
rubrics_metrics.description: Topics and beats that historically lead to subscriber interest and signups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A selection criterion for future coverage prioritization tied to business goals (subscriber growth).

rubrics_metrics.name: Author/byline performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance metrics specific to authors (how stories by an author perform).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to allocate assignments and prioritize stories based on individual author audience pull.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline format performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Which headline styles/formats produce better engagement or clicks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalizes headline testing into editorial practice for maximizing CTR and suitability for distribution channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real-time CTR
rubrics_metrics.description: Click-through rate measured in real time for stories (used especially for homepage decisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to decide 'What Goes on the Homepage?' — a fast signal on initial appeal that can inform placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Velocity of pickup
rubrics_metrics.description: Speed and intensity with which a story is picked up by audiences or other outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homepage and promotion criterion: rapid early traction can justify prominent placement or further investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted dwell time
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecasted time users will spend on a story (used for homepage selection and recommendation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalized as a predictor of depth/value; appears both as a metric and as an implicit newsworthiness signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-section of topics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix of topics shown together to provide breadth on front pages or homepages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Homepage curation principle to ensure topical diversity and balance rather than a single-topic dominance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subscriber-only content (promotion priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Content restricted to subscribers that may be prioritized for promotion to retain/convert paying readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'What Should Get Promotional Push?' — such content may be given editorial/promotion resources to maximize subscriber value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original investigations (promotion priority)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive investigative reporting recommended for promotional push.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valued for brand mission and likely long-term impact; often prioritized even if short-term metrics are modest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content with high quality reads + low natural traffic
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories that achieve strong quality reads but receive low organic traffic (candidates for promotion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotional priority given to content demonstrating depth engagement but lacking discovery; promotion can amplify value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click optimization vs mission alignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension between optimizing for clicks and aligning with journalistic mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as a central editorial tension; requires balancing short-term attention metrics against longer-term values and public interest journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-term metrics vs subscriber lifetime value
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension between chasing immediate metric gains and focusing on long-term subscriber value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for trade-offs in prioritization — e.g., sacrificing some short-term clicks to build subscriber trust and retention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative dashboard vs qualitative editorial judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension between relying on analytics dashboards and exercising human editorial judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights limits of metrics and the need to retain qualitative newsroom expertise alongside data-driven signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic homogenization vs distinctive voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension where algorithmic optimization can make content homogeneous, undermining a newsroom's distinctive voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns against over-optimization that risks losing brand differentiation and editorial identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted CTR
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecasted click-through rate used as an implicit newsworthiness criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in 'Implicit Newsworthiness Criteria from Metrics' — used to judge 'clickability' and selection probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted shareability
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecast of how likely content is to be shared across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion for potential reach and earned distribution; influences headline and social copy choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted subscriber retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecast of a story's effect on retaining subscribers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to prioritize stories that contribute to long-term revenue and relationship value, beyond immediate metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted recirculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Forecast of a story's ability to pull readers deeper into the site (recirculation potential).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit newsworthiness signal related to site engagement architecture and internal traffic generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic + format match to audience segment
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which topic and storytelling format align with a specific audience segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to target content to segments, increasing relevance and engagement (audience-segmentation informed coverage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-of-day fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Matching content timing to audience behavior patterns (when audiences are active).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operationalized as an implicit criterion for scheduling and promotion to maximize reach and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic targeting fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Relevance of a story to the geographic distribution of the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit criterion informing localization and targeting strategies for both homepage placement and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline match to query trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which a headline aligns with current search/query trends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to improve discoverability via search and match user intent; ties SEO signals to editorial headline choices.
